title: SLI bucketing and eviction prioritization policy for latency-sensitive model variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As adoption of low-latency variants grows (short-sequence chat, streaming tokens), we need a deterministic, per-variant SLI bucketing strategy combined with a regional eviction prioritization policy. This ticket defines SLI buckets (latency/availability/quality), error-budget actions, and precise eviction ordering to be used by the smart-router and the Dedicated autoscaler.

Goals: Define measurable SLI buckets per endpoint/model-variant, map error-budget burn to automated actions (circuit-breaker, progressive rollback, regional failover), and codify an eviction priority list that reduces customer-visible degradation while preserving overall throughput. Provide clear observability and rollout steps for safe deployment.

Scope: - SLI bucketing for latency-sensitive variants (p50/p95/p99 and streaming token latency) - Availability SLI for model instance failures and RPC errors - Error-budget policy mapping to automated mitigations - Eviction prioritization across model variants and regions - Integration points for smart-router and Console dashboards.

Out of scope: Changes to model training/eval processes, deep changes to billing, and wholesale redesign of autoscaler heuristics (only policy hooks).
acceptance_criteria: Defined SLI buckets and thresholds documented for at least three representative variant classes (low-latency, standard, high-throughput)

Automated policy mapping implemented in smart-router (feature-flagged) that triggers: slow-path routing, model variant fallback, regional re-routing, and circuit-breaker short-circuiting based on error-budget status
Eviction priority table implemented and validated in Dedicated autoscaler simulator (results show <=10% customer-visible error-rate increase in high-load scenario versus baseline)
Console dashboard tiles created: per-variant error budget burn, per-region capacity headroom, and circuit-breaker history with links to playbook
Runbook and canary rollout plan executed in staging and validated by SRE and a product representative
monitoring: Primary SLIs: request_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), streaming_token_latency_ms (p50/p95), success_rate (2xx responses), downstream_model_error_rate (500/4xx). Secondary: queue_length, avg_batch_size, kv_cache_hit_rate. Dashboards: runtime-1.22 -> Variant SLI Overview, Region Capacity Heatmap, Error Budget Burn Explorer.
error_budget_policy: Buckets: green (<=20% burn), watch (20-50%), probing (50-80%), critical (>80%). Actions: green -> no change; watch -> enable prefix caching and increase batching window by 10% for non-streaming routes; probing -> enable variant fallback to quantized model (same output schema) and cap concurrency per-customer by 25%; critical -> trigger circuit-breaker for affected variant in the region and initiate cross-region failover ordering. All actions are reversible and logged in Console with links to audit events.
circuit_breaker_thresholds: Soft trip: 5xx rate >1.5% over 5m OR p99 latency >1200ms over 5m. Hard trip: 5xx rate >3% over 1m OR sustained error-budget burn >90% for 10m. Soft trip triggers gradual throttling and invocation of fallback model; hard trip opens the breaker and routes traffic to next-priority region/variant.
eviction_policy_summary: Eviction priority (highest to lowest preservation): 1) Pinned high-SLA customer variants (never evicted unless region-level catastrophe). 2) Latency-sensitive cached variants (preserve cache-serving nodes; only evict stateless evaluators). 3) Low-cost quantized fallbacks (evict before full-precision variants to free GPU memory for high-quality variants). 4) Background batch/async jobs and pre-warming instances. Regional ordering: prefer evicting in non-primary replica regions first, preserving primary until capacity is exhausted. Tie-breakers: minimize customer impact by selecting least recently used variants with lowest active concurrency. This policy is expressed as a simple priority score used by autoscaler and smart-router.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Feature-flagged implementation in smart-router; unit + integration tests; staging deployment
Week 2: Run autoscaler simulator with recorded traffic (shadow policy) and compare against baseline for 3 failure scenarios
Week 3: Canary in US-east region for internal traffic (5% p95 of production); monitor error-budget and circuit-breaker logs
Week 4: Expand to US-west and EU regions (25% traffic), runbook dry-run with SRE on-call
Week 5: Full rollout and retrospective; mark policies as default for runtime-1.22
risks_mitigations: Risk: Fallback variants may produce degraded outputs leading to quality regression. Mitigation: bind each fallback to a quality threshold and enable immediate rollback if regression is detected by prompt-based evals.
Risk: Oscillation between regions if error budgets are repaired too quickly. Mitigation: introduce cooldown windows (10m) before re-routing back to previously evicted region.
Risk: Over-eager eviction impacting pinned enterprise customers. Mitigation: honor pin annotations and shield top-tier customers from autoscale-driven eviction unless explicit override by SRE.
